props.title: The Set-Up
props.initialSlug: Aging boxer risks all for one final brutal fight

sections.content: **The Set-Up** (1949) revolutionized boxing films by unfolding in real-time across 72 brutal minutes, following aging prizefighter Stoker Thompson's fateful night in Paradise City. Director Robert Wise crafted a noir masterpiece that influenced countless sports films, from **Raging Bull** (1980) to **Creed** (2015). The film's gritty authenticity and innovative storytelling stripped away boxing movie glamour, revealing the sport's desperate underbelly decades before **Rocky** (1976) romanticized the underdog story.

sections.content: Film noir's influence permeates every frame of **The Set-Up**, with cinematographer Milton Krasner's high-contrast lighting turning the boxing arena into a gladiatorial colosseum of shadows. The film's innovative structure - showing events in real-time - created unbearable tension that later influenced **High Noon** (1952) and **12 Angry Men** (1957). Robert Ryan's performance as Stoker Thompson draws from his real-life boxing experience at Dartmouth, lending authenticity rarely seen in previous boxing films.

The film's exploration of masculinity and desperation echoes through later works like **Fat City** (1972) and **The Wrestler** (2008). Wise's decision to show the brutality of boxing without glamorization created a template for realistic sports films, influencing everything from **Somebody Up There Likes Me** (1956) to **Million Dollar Baby** (2004). The cramped, sweaty locker room scenes became a standard for depicting boxing's backstage reality. SUBHEAD: Impact on Modern Boxing Films

sections.content: Modern boxing films like **Southpaw** (2015) and **Bleed for This** (2016) owe a significant debt to **The Set-Up**'s unflinching portrayal of boxing's physical and psychological toll. The film's innovative use of diegetic sound - crowd noise, punch impacts, corner instructions - created an immersive experience that became standard practice in sports filmmaking, perfected in films like **Ali** (2001) and **Cinderella Man** (2005).
